name: Karakol Gorge
full: Karakol Gorge (Karakol canyon, Karakol Nature Park)
near: Karakol — the entrance to the gorge is 3–7 km south of the town (too.kg: “3 km south of Karakol”; the Ala-Kul trailhead at the “first bridge” is ~7 km from the last stop of marshrutka No. 101).
elev: Gorge entrance ~1,900–2,000 m (Nomad's Land: the park at 2,000 m), ski base 2,300 m, Lake Ala-Kul 3,532 m (ecostan.kg; kaktus.media gives 3,440 m), Ala-Kul Pass ~3,900 m. The earlier figure “3,532 m” referred to the lake, not the gorge.
short: The 40-km gorge of the Karakol River just south of the town of Karakol — the core of Karakol Nature Park (1997): spruce forests, an alpine camp, a ski base and the start of trails to Lake Ala-Kul and Altyn-Arashan.
desc: The gorge cuts through the eastern part of the Terskey Ala-Too from the outskirts of Karakol to the glaciers beneath the peaks of Karakol (5,281 m), Jigit (5,170 m) and Przhevalsky (4,283 m). This is the territory of Karakol State Nature Park (38,134 ha, established 15.04.1997): more than 300–700 plant species, snow leopard, golden eagle, and the saker falcon, listed in the Red Book. In the lower part there is the Karakol ski base (2,300 m, cable cars); higher up there are a summer alpine camp, yurt camps (Sirota) and trails: Kyrgyzstan's most popular trek, Karakol — Ala-Kul — Altyn-Arashan (3 days, 50–55 km, a 3,900 m pass). Since 2025 an eco post has operated at the entrance with a vehicle fee; the walk-in park entrance fee is 250–300 som per person according to 2025 guidebooks.
guide: Karakol Gorge is the very “front door” to Ala-Kul: from the last stop of marshrutka No. 101 to the first bridge it is another 7 km, so arrange a taxi to the bridge or to the alpine camp. If you aren't doing a multi-day trek, make a day loop: 10 km and 400 m of gain to the alpine camp through spruce forest with views of Przhevalsky Peak. In winter the same gorge is a ski area at 2,300 m with a view of Issyk-Kul; in summer the lift carries only groups. Pay the eco fee at the post (keep the receipt — it is checked on the trail) and don't count on mobile coverage above the base. In the evening go back to Karakol for ashlan-fu and Dungan cuisine.
see: Spruce forests and alpine meadows; the Karakol ski base (2,300 m) with a panorama of the town and the lake; the alpine camp and the Sirota yurt camp; waterfalls and moraine lakes in the upper reaches; the side valleys of Kashka-Suu and On-Tor; the route to Lake Ala-Kul (3,532 m) and over the pass to Altyn-Arashan; the peaks of Karakol, Jigit and Przhevalsky.
skip: You are not ready for a mountain trail — without strong legs the gorge is limited to the road up to the ski base. You have one day and want “postcard” views without effort — then Jeti-Oguz or Altyn-Arashan by SUV is easier. You've come in the shoulder season (April–May, October–November): the passes are under snow and the camps are closed.
diff: The lower part (up to the ski base/alpine camp) is easy: dirt road/trail, 10 km and +400 m to the alpine camp in 4–5 h (Destination Karakol). The Ala-Kul trek is hard: 3 days, 50–55 km, a 3,900 m pass (Snoezels on the road).
when: Trekking — mid-June to mid-September (Destination Karakol, Snoezels); July–August are the most stable. Ski base — December–March. In autumn (September) — golden larches and fewer people.
hours: Google Maps (03.10.2026): open 24 hours. The nature park's eco post at the entrance works daily (Sputnik, November 2025). The ski base and the alpine camp are seasonal.
daytime: Morning: set off on the trail before 9:00 to get through the forest before the midday heat and reach the camp before the thunderstorm (downpours are common in the afternoon in July–August).
how: From Karakol: marshrutka No. 101 from the city bus station to the terminus at the gorge entrance (10–20 som, 2025), then ~7 km on foot or by taxi to the “first bridge”/alpine camp; shared taxi ~200 som per person (backpackmoments, 2025). SUV transfer to the Ala-Kul trailhead — myway.kg. From Bishkek: marshrutka/taxi to Karakol (Bishkek bus station, 1/1 Alma-Atinskaya St., 6–8 h), then as above.
needcar: Not necessary: marshrutka No. 101 takes you to the park entrance; but to reach the start of the trail (7 km) a taxi or SUV is more convenient.
self: Yes: the Ala-Kul trail is marked and can be followed with maps.me; no permits are needed (not a border zone), only the park eco fee. Book yurt camps through CBT Karakol.
roadtype: Paved road through the town to the outskirts, then a gravel/dirt road through the gorge to the ski base and the alpine camp (passable by a passenger car up to the base, above that an SUV, too.kg); after that — mountain trails. You cannot drive to Ala-Kul.
traveltime: Karakol — park entrance: 15–20 min by marshrutka No. 101. To the alpine camp on foot from the first bridge: 10 km, +400 m, 4–5 h (Destination Karakol). To Ala-Kul: 2 days, to Altyn-Arashan — 3 days (50–55 km).
stay: In the gorge: the alpine camp (in summer), the Sirota yurt camp (day 1 of the trek), tent camps at Ala-Kul (booking through CBT Karakol), a hotel at the Karakol ski base (in winter). Camp prices are not published in the sources (“more expensive than the national average” — wanderlustdesigners, 2025). City base — Karakol: hostels and guesthouses from ~800–1,500 som (rough figure, not verified).
net: There is coverage at the entrance and at the ski base (outskirts of Karakol); higher up the gorge and along the whole Ala-Kul trek there is no signal (too.kg; wanderlustdesigners 2025: “there will be no signal for the whole trek”). Offline maps are a must.
entry: On foot: 250 som per person (visitkarakol.com; backpackmoments, 01.2025) — 300 som according to other reports (Snoezels on the road). Vehicles at the eco post since November 2025: passenger car — 200 som, truck/bus — 800 som (Sputnik Kyrgyzstan, 02.11.2025). Sputnik does not mention a separate rate for foreigners; gokyrgyzstan.info writes “$5 per person, $10 per car” (date not given).
transfer: Marshrutka No. 101 — 10–20 som (2025). Shared taxi to the bridge ~200 som/person (2025). SUV Karakol — Ala-Kul trailhead: 9,500–17,600 som per car (MYWAY.kg, 2026).
bring: Trekking boots, rain jacket, a warm layer (around 0 °C at night in the camps even in summer), sun protection, cash for the eco fee and camps, an offline map, a filter/water purification tablets (boil river water — too.kg), a food supply — there are no shops in the gorge.
warn: The eco fee is mandatory and the receipt is checked on the trail; there is a separate fee for entering by car. There is no mobile coverage above the base. Ala-Kul Pass (3,900 m) — altitude sickness and snow until the end of June; downpours and thunderstorms in the afternoon; solo hikers should register at the camp. In spring and after rain — rockfalls and fords.
food: In the gorge — only what the yurt camps cook (dinner/breakfast included). In Karakol: ashlan-fu (cold Dungan noodles, rows of stalls at the bazaar), Dungan dishes, lagman, manty, boorsoki — specific eateries have not been verified.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 68 ratings (03.10.2026). Typical pros from 2024–2025 blogs: accessibility from the town, a marked trail, views from Ala-Kul; cons — paid entry, expensive yurt camps, no mobile coverage, 7 km from the marshrutka terminus to the trail.
p.sum: Your base is the town of Karakol: it is 3–7 km to the entrance of the nature park (marshrutka No. 101 or a taxi), and a per-person and per-vehicle fee is paid at the eco post. For a day trip a taxi to the “first bridge” (~2,000 som) and a walk to the alpine camp are enough; for the Ala-Kul trek, order an SUV to the alpine camp/second bridge (8,000–15,000 som per car) and rent gear from EcoTrek/4Rent. Overnight stays — the Sirota yurt camp (~$45 with dinner and breakfast) or a tent; in winter — the Karakol ski base, 7 km from the town.

p.iti.0.title: A day from Karakol
p.iti.0.plan: 8:00 taxi to the first bridge (~2,000 som) → walk through the spruce forest to the alpine camp (10 km, +400 m) or to Sirota → lunch at Sirota → descend, taxi back by 18:00; in winter — a day at the ski base.
p.iti.1.title: Ala-Kul in 2 days
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: SUV to the alpine camp (2 h) → Sirota (overnight in a yurt). Day 2: climb to Ala-Kul (3–4 h), rest, descend to the alpine camp and transfer to Karakol.
p.iti.2.title: Classic 3–4 days
p.iti.2.plan: Karakol → Sirota → Ala-Kul → pass → Altyn-Arashan (hot springs, yurt ~2,800 som with dinner and bathing) → Ak-Suu → marshrutka 30–50 som to Karakol. Combine with Jeti-Oguz and the Przhevalsky Museum.
p.season: December–March — ski season (usually from late November, in 2025 — from 6 December). April–May — shoulder season, mud, the pass is closed. Mid-June–September — trekking; July–August is peak crowds and afternoon thunderstorms; September — golden larches, cold nights. October–May on the pass −25…−30 °C, only for the well prepared. Ticks in the spruce forest — May–June.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka No. 101 20 + on foot; eco fee ~250–300; own tent/rental ~1,500/day for a set; camping 100–300; own food ~600/day. A 3-day trek ≈ 5,000–7,000 som/person (excluding the trip from Bishkek).
p.budget.comfort: SUV 9,500–15,000 som/car (÷4 ≈ 2,500–3,800); Sirota $45 (~3,900 som); guide $50–80/day; horse $100+/day. A 3-day trek ≈ 25,000–45,000 som/person.
p.permits: No border-zone permit needed. Karakol Nature Park: eco fee for walkers ~250–300 som (2024–2025 guides), for a car 200 som (eco post since 11.2025); keep the receipt — it is checked on the trail. Payment at the eco post is in cash.
p.access: With kids — the ski base and a walk to the first bridge; the Ala-Kul trek is for teenagers with experience. For older people — only the road section. Wheelchair — no (dirt). With a dog — allowed on the trail, but there are shepherd dogs at the camps; the park rules on dogs were not found.
